column1: # What a greyed item says, and where it takes you: one row for each reason something is off because of a setting or a
# sign-in. The portal's pickers (portal/static/answers.js: the Terminal's Open menu, Chat's Who answers), Home and
# Settings read it through /api/answers (portal/portal/answers.py setup_links); the Code page (its model picker's Who
# answers, its terminal panel's Open…, the mode picker, previews, folders) has the same rows in
# code/web/src/setuplinks.ts (tests compare the two). Each greyed item says where it is turned on and takes you there:
# a link or a menu item of its own, or — in a menu — a button beside it ("Go to Settings"), never a change of the menu.
#   target   setting:KEY — the portal's Settings at that row (scrolled to, highlighted; a switch of its own focused:
#            a key of catalog/settings.tsv), or at one of the page's own rows (setting:+project-folders …: the row) |
#            signin:terminal — the tool itself in the terminal, where its own sign-in starts | signin:chat — Settings ›
#            Your AI subscriptions, at that tool's Chat row with its Sign in open
#   where    where it takes you, in a few words (a button's name: "Go to Settings › …")
#   says     one sentence: what is off, and where it is turned on — "turns it on" where that row does, "shows how to
#            turn it on" where the row is read-only (a step in a terminal), and "from the computer running DevOS ADE"
#            wherever only that computer may (a read-only row's step, a local setting, one turned on only there, a
#            Chat sign-in's command) — the page shows it as the item's words
